Campus-to-Corporate Transformation
# The engineer who learned to read people.
How curiosity, not a career plan, shaped a leader.
Ask Srikanth Kalyanasundaram to describe himself in one word, and he does not reach for a job title. He calls himself dynamic. Over three decades spanning shop floors, boardrooms, and classrooms, he has been a mechanical engineer who chose people over machines, an HR leader who never lost the engineer's instinct for process, and a mentor who insists he learns as much from students as they learn from him. His twelve-week experiential programme helps young people bridge the gap between classroom expectations and workplace reality, using a skill matrix that makes the gap between where a student is and where they want to be visible and actionable.

The gap we close
## Degrees prove knowledge. Placements demand something more.
Students leave campus technically capable but often unprepared for the interview room and the first ninety days on the job, the etiquette, the communication under pressure, the composure. That gap is exactly what employers screen for, and exactly what a lecture cannot fix. It has to be practised.

The signature programme
## Mindful Professional 360°
A structured, twelve-week journey across six pillars, combining professional skills, leadership, and emotional resilience through live practice and corporate simulation, not slides.
Pillar 01
### Professional Excellence
Corporate etiquette, business communication, and presentation, the everyday signals that mark someone as ready.
Pillar 02
### Career Readiness
Resume and LinkedIn, mock interviews, group discussions, and structured problem solving.
Pillar 03
### Leadership Skills
Critical thinking, decision making, and teamwork practised in real scenarios, not theory.
Pillar 04
### Emotional Intelligence
Self-awareness, giving and receiving feedback, and managing pressure in high-stakes moments.
Pillar 05
### Mindfulness Practices
Focus and composure that turn interview anxiety into calm, credible performance.
Pillar 06
### Corporate Simulations
Boardroom, client, and crisis scenarios, gamified, so students rehearse the job before they get it.

Why it works
## Human-led. AI-augmented. Genuinely experiential.
Tools can drill answers. They cannot replicate a room full of peers reacting in real time, a mentor reading the moment, or the muscle memory built by doing the hard thing under pressure. That is where confidence is actually made.
- Live simulations and role-play, facilitated by a senior practitioner
- Peer feedback and group dynamics that mirror a real workplace
- AI-based practice between sessions, so live time is spent on what only humans can teach

Srikanth began his career as a mechanical engineer on the shop floor before transitioning to lead HR operations as Deputy General Manager at John Cockerill. With over two decades in HR leadership across manufacturing and engineering, he designs training programs using a recruiter's eye and a coach's perspective.

FAQ
## Common questions
### What does Srikanth Kalyanasundaram offer?
People advisory and transformation in four practices: Campus (campus-to-corporate readiness for colleges and graduate trainees), Respect (POSH compliance, workplace dignity and culture), Inspire (leadership development, mentoring, wellbeing and personal effectiveness) and Benefits (independent employee benefits advice for employers). Sessions are delivered on campus and on site across India.
### What is the Mindful Professional 360° programme?
A 12-week experiential campus-to-corporate programme across six pillars: professional excellence, career readiness, leadership skills, emotional intelligence, mindfulness practices and corporate simulations. Every student is assessed at the start and the end, and the institution receives a placement readiness report.
### Can a college start with a short pilot?
Yes. Most colleges begin with a two-day campus sprint for one cohort, which produces a readiness snapshot, and then decide on evidence whether to run the full 12-week programme across the placement season.
### Do you run POSH training for colleges and universities?
Yes. The POSH engagement covers student awareness sessions, faculty and staff orientation, Internal Committee member training, a review of the policy and process, and an annual refresher cycle. Srikanth is a certified POSH trainer through the Indian Society for Training and Development.
### What is a graduate trainee bootcamp?
A two to three day immersive programme at intake for cohorts of new graduate hires, covering business communication, workplace etiquette, emotional intelligence and realistic workplace simulations, tailored to the company's onboarding goals.
### Do you sell insurance as part of employee benefits advice?
No. Employee benefits work is independent advice only. No insurance is sold, solicited or arranged, and no commission is taken from insurers or brokers. Where a policy is needed, the employer's IRDAI-licensed broker places it.
### Where are sessions delivered, and in which languages?
Srikanth is based in Mumbai and delivers on campus and on site across India. He works in English, Hindi, Tamil, Malayalam and Marathi.
### How do I book a consultation?
Use the enquiry form on the contact page or write to mtmdselflove@gmail.com. Most engagements start with a 15 minute intro call, and scope, schedule and fees are agreed in writing before any work begins.
## Bring the programme to your campus or team.
Start with a short conversation. We will map your placement or onboarding goals and design a pilot that proves the value before any long-term commitment.
Book a 15 minute intro call Request a brochure

About the Founder
# Srikanth Kalyanasundaram
Srikanth Kalyanasundaram is a dynamic HR leader, entrepreneur, and mentor who has spent over two decades building people-centred, high-performance organisations.
- The Background: Started as a mechanical engineer but chose people over machines, retaining a sharp, analytical instinct for process.
- The Philosophy: A lifelong educator who believes mentoring is a two-way street, learning just as much from his students as they do from him.
- The Mission: Helping the next generation cross the bridge from campus to corporate.

The practitioner
## Two decades inside the hiring machine.
Srikanth has led HR operations, talent acquisition, performance management, employee engagement, learning and development, compensation and benefits, compliance, and HR digitalisation across leading manufacturing and engineering organisations. He has aligned human-capital strategy with business goals, driven organisational effectiveness, and built high-performance workplace cultures.
A strong advocate of digital transformation, he has led implementations of HRIS, SuccessFactors, and HCM platforms, improving process automation, efficiency, and the everyday employee experience. Across his career he has delivered measurable impact through workforce optimisation, policy innovation, and employee wellbeing.
Beyond corporate leadership, he is deeply committed to mentoring professionals, promoting mindful leadership, and building positive workplace ecosystems, the conviction that now drives his campus-to-corporate work.

Title: Mindful Professional 360° Programme | Srikanth Kalyanasundaram
Description: A 12-week experiential campus-to-corporate programme across six pillars, from professional excellence and career readiness to corporate simulations.

The Signature Programme
# Mindful Professional 360°
A twelve-week transformation journey that rehearses the corporate world before students step into it, six pillars, taught through live practice, feedback, and simulation.
Book a Consultation Bring it to your campus
12
weeks, structured week by week
6
pillars of transformation
100%
experiential, practice over lecture
What it covers
## Six pillars that make a graduate ready.
Each pillar is built around doing, not listening. Students practise, get feedback, and repeat, the way real skill is formed.
Pillar 01
### Professional Excellence
Corporate etiquette, business communication, and presentation skills. How to write, speak, dress, and carry oneself so that competence is visible from the first minute.
Pillar 02
### Career Readiness
Resume and LinkedIn that get shortlisted, structured problem solving, group discussions, and mock interviews with real, specific feedback.
Pillar 03
### Leadership Skills
Critical thinking, decision making under constraints, and teamwork, practised through tasks that reward judgment, not memorisation.
Pillar 04
### Emotional Intelligence
Self-awareness, reading a room, giving and receiving feedback, and staying steady when the stakes and the pressure rise.
Pillar 05
### Mindfulness Practices
Focus, clarity, and composure. Practical techniques that convert interview nerves into calm, credible presence, and prevent burnout later.
Pillar 06
### Corporate Simulations
Boardroom debates, client conversations, and crisis scenarios, gamified role-play so students have already "been there" before day one on the job.
The journey
## Twelve weeks, one arc.
A suggested structure. The sequence is tailored to each cohort's starting point and placement calendar.
Weeks 1 to 2
### Foundation & self-awareness
Baseline assessment, personal goals, and the mindset shift from student to professional. Where do you stand today, and where are you headed?
Weeks 3 to 4
### Communication & etiquette
Business communication, professional writing, and the everyday etiquette that shapes first impressions.
Weeks 5 to 6
### Presence & presentation
Public speaking, structured presentation, and executive presence, rehearsed and recorded for feedback.
Weeks 7 to 8
### Emotional intelligence & mindfulness
Managing pressure, self-regulation, and focus practices that hold up in real interviews and real work.
Weeks 9 to 10
### Leadership & problem solving
Critical thinking, decision making, and teamwork through case-based and simulated challenges.
Weeks 11 to 12
### Corporate simulations & interviews
Full mock interviews, group discussions, and corporate scenario simulations. Final readiness assessment and report.

Confidence is hard to see, so we make it visible. Each student is assessed at the start and again at the end, and each institution receives a readiness report it can stand behind.
- Baseline and final readiness assessment for every student
- A cohort-level report for placement teams and accreditation narratives

For Colleges & Universities

Your students have the degrees. We give them the confidence, communication, and composure that convert interviews into offers, and give your placement team something measurable to show for it.
Request a pilot See the programme
The placement officer's reality
## The technical box is ticked. The rest decides the offer.
Recruiters rarely reject your students on aptitude. They reject on the interview, hesitant communication, weak group discussions, visible nerves, and a gap in professional maturity. That is coachable, but only through practice, and only if someone in the room has actually sat on the other side of the hiring table.
- Students who freeze in interviews despite strong marks
- Group discussions that go quiet or turn chaotic
- Placement statistics that plateau year after year
- Accreditation narratives that need evidence, not adjectives
Led by someone who has hired
### A hiring insider, not a lecturer
Srikanth spent over two decades in HR leadership across industry, setting the very bars your students are trying to clear. Your cohort learns what recruiters actually look for, from someone who used to be the recruiter.
About Srikanth →

01

03
### Accreditation support
Documented skill development and outcomes that strengthen NAAC and NBA narratives around student preparedness.
04
### Resilient students
Mindfulness and emotional-intelligence practices that reduce interview anxiety and support student wellbeing.
05
### Flexible delivery
A two-day sprint, or the full twelve-week journey across the placement season, designed around your calendar.

### A senior name attached
An award-winning HR leader associated with your placement effort, reassuring to students, parents, and recruiters alike.

The onboarding gap
## The first ninety days are expensive.
A graduate trainee who cannot yet communicate with clients, manage feedback, or navigate workplace norms takes months to become productive, and is more likely to leave. A focused, experiential bootcamp at intake changes that curve.
- Trainees hesitant in client and cross-team communication
- Managers spending time on basics instead of the work
- Early attrition eroding the cost of hiring and training
- Inconsistent professional standards across a cohort
The corporate bootcamp
## An immersion designed around your outcomes.
01
### Faster time-to-productivity
Trainees arrive on the floor already fluent in communication, etiquette, and professional judgment.
02
### Stronger early retention
Emotional-intelligence and resilience practices help new hires settle, cope, and stay.
03
### Consistent standards
A whole cohort brought to a common professional baseline, regardless of which campus they came from.
04
### Real simulations
Client conversations, team scenarios, and pressure situations rehearsed before they happen for real.
05
### Senior facilitation
Led by an HR leader who has run onboarding and L&D at scale inside industry.
06
### Tailored, not templated
Built to your sector, your values, and the specific gaps in your incoming cohort.

URL: https://srikanthk.pages.dev/posh
Title: POSH Training for Colleges & Universities | Srikanth Kalyanasundaram
Description: POSH awareness for students, faculty and staff, Internal Committee training and policy review for colleges in India, by an ISTD-certified POSH trainer.

POSH for Institutions
# Compliance is annual. Behaviour is the point.
Most campuses can produce a policy document. Fewer can show that students, faculty and committee members actually understand what to do when something happens. That gap is what these sessions close.
Book a 15 minute intro call What is delivered
Why this recurs every year
## A standing obligation, not a one-time certificate.
The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 requires an employer to constitute an Internal Committee and to carry out regular awareness and orientation programmes. Higher educational institutions additionally sit under the UGC Regulations, 2015. Both frameworks assume an ongoing cycle of training and reporting rather than a single sign-off.
In practice that means new student intakes every year, committee members who rotate, and staff who joined after the last session. The obligation renews itself, which is exactly why it suits an annual engagement.
Your compliance team should confirm the specific requirements that apply to your institution. Scope is set against that, not against a template.
Delivered by a practitioner
### Someone who has run this inside a company
Srikanth is a certified POSH trainer through the Indian Society for Training and Development, and has led HR operations and compliance inside a large engineering organisation where this framework is live rather than theoretical. Sessions are built around real situations and the questions people are actually afraid to ask.
About Srikanth →
The engagement
## Five components, scoped to your campus.
01
### Student awareness sessions
Batch-wise sessions in plain language: what the law covers, what it does not, how to raise a concern, and what happens next. Built for people who will not read a policy PDF.
02
### Faculty and staff orientation
Separate session for teaching and non-teaching staff, covering their own obligations, how to receive a disclosure, and what not to do in the first conversation.
03
### Internal Committee training
Working session for committee members on inquiry process, documentation, confidentiality, principles of natural justice, and the practical mistakes that undo an otherwise sound inquiry.
04
### Policy and process review
A read of your existing policy, committee composition, reporting routes and record keeping, with a short written note on gaps and what to change first.
05
### Annual refresher cycle
An agreed calendar for the next intake and the next committee rotation, so the obligation is scheduled rather than remembered.
06
### Combined with readiness work
Institutions often pair this with the campus-to-corporate programme, since both run on the academic calendar and reach the same cohorts.
How it starts
## Three steps, no obligation.
01
### A short call
Fifteen minutes on your student numbers, committee status, and when your academic calendar allows sessions.
02
### A scoped proposal
Which components you need, how many batches, over how many days, and what it costs. One page.
03
### Deliver, then schedule the next cycle
Sessions run, the written note follows, and next year goes on the calendar before this year closes.
## Get the annual cycle off your to-do list.
Start with a short call about your campus, your committee, and your calendar.

Title: Leadership Coaching & HR Advisory | Srikanth Kalyanasundaram
Description: One to one leadership coaching for professionals, and retained HR advisory for organisations: operations, talent, performance, culture and HR systems.

Advisory & Coaching
# The work that does not fit in a workshop.
Some problems need a room full of people and a curriculum. Others need one person, one hour at a time, over months. This is the second kind: one to one coaching, and advisory that stays with an organisation long enough to see a decision through.
Book a 15 minute intro call See the two tracks
Track one
## Mindful leadership coaching, one to one.
For professionals and senior leaders working on clarity rather than technique. Typical reasons people start: a step up into a role that needs more presence than expertise, a decision that has been pending too long, or the particular flatness that arrives after a long run of delivery.
- Career clarity and the next move, thought through rather than reacted to
- Executive presence: how you enter a room, hold a position, and handle being disagreed with
- Composure under sustained load, using mindfulness as a working tool rather than a retreat
- Direct work with Srikanth throughout, with no associate handover
Happiness Coaching, Berkeley Institute of Well Being Mindfulness Coaching, Happiitude Business Storytelling, NIST
Track two
## Retained HR advisory.
For organisations that need senior HR judgement regularly, but not a full time senior HR hire.
Operations
### HR operations and policy
Process design, policy drafting and review, compliance routines, and the unglamorous work of making HR run predictably.
Talent
### Hiring and performance
Talent acquisition, performance management frameworks, compensation benchmarking, and onboarding that does not lose people in the first ninety days.
Systems
### HR digitalisation
Selection and rollout of HRIS and HCM platforms, including SAP SuccessFactors, with attention to adoption rather than configuration alone.
Culture
### Engagement and retention
Diagnosing why people actually leave, and the small number of changes that move it. Culture work with a measurable target, not a values poster.
Compliance
### POSH and ESG
POSH framework setup and committee training, and ESG reporting groundwork from a people and governance angle.
Onboarding
### Group onboarding design
Designing intake programmes for cohorts rather than individuals, drawing on a flagship group onboarding programme built and run inside a large engineering organisation.
Shapes
## Three ways this usually runs.
01
### A single session
One conversation on a specific decision. Useful when you want a second opinion from outside your own organisation, and nothing more.
02
### A block of sessions
A set number of coaching conversations over a few months, with an agreed focus at the start and a review at the end.
03
### A monthly retainer
A fixed amount of senior HR time each month for organisations that would rather have judgement on call than a project.
Scope and fees are set per engagement. Ask on the intro call.
## Start with a conversation, not a proposal.
Fifteen minutes is usually enough to tell whether this is the right kind of help.

Title: Employee Benefits Advisory | Srikanth Kalyanasundaram
Description: Independent employee benefits advice for employers in India: benefits design, employee wellbeing and benefits governance. Advice only; no insurance is sold.

Employee Benefits
# Benefits your people understand, use and value.
Advice for employers on designing, running and governing employee benefits and wellbeing, from an HR leader who has led compensation and benefits inside large manufacturing and engineering organisations.
Book a 15 minute intro call See the three areas
What we advise on
## Three areas, one goal: benefits that earn their cost.
Many organisations spend well on benefits and still hear that employees do not know what they have. The work is to close that gap.
01
### Employee benefits advisory
A review of what you offer today against what your workforce actually needs: leave, health cover structure, family and flexible benefits, and how each is explained to employees. Recommendations you can act on, with priorities and trade-offs set out plainly.
02
### Employee wellbeing
Wellbeing programmes that go beyond an annual health camp: stress and resilience sessions, mindfulness at work, manager guidance for wellbeing conversations, and a simple way to see whether the programme is used.
03
### Benefits operations and governance
Clear benefits policies, an annual benefits review, enrolment and grievance processes that work, criteria for evaluating benefit providers, and a calendar for statutory benefit obligations such as gratuity and maternity benefit.
Independent advice only. We do not sell, solicit or arrange insurance, and we take no commission from insurers or brokers. Where an insurance policy is needed, we work alongside your IRDAI-licensed insurance broker, or suggest that you appoint one.
How we work on benefits
Shapes
## Three ways this usually runs.
01
### A benefits health check
A short review of your current benefits, policies and employee feedback, ending in a written summary of what to keep, fix and add.
02
### A design project
Redesigning a benefits or wellbeing programme from the brief to the rollout plan, including how it is explained to employees.
03
### An annual governance review
A yearly review of policies, provider performance and statutory obligations, for organisations that want a standing outside view.
Scope and fees are set per engagement. Ask on the intro call.
FAQ
## Questions employers ask
### What does employee benefits advisory cover?
A review of the benefits an employer offers against what its workforce needs, the design of benefits and wellbeing programmes, clear benefits policies and processes, criteria for evaluating benefit providers, and a calendar for statutory benefit obligations.
### Who is it for?
Employers and HR teams in India that want an independent, outside view of their employee benefits and wellbeing, without hiring a full time benefits specialist.
### Do you sell or arrange insurance?
No. This is advice only. No insurance is sold, solicited or arranged, and no commission is taken from insurers or brokers. Where a policy is needed, the employer's IRDAI-licensed broker places it.

Title: Insights on Leadership & People Skills | Srikanth Kalyanasundaram
Description: Selected writing by Srikanth Kalyanasundaram on leadership presence, people skills, culture, mindful leadership and the move from campus to corporate.

Insights
# Notes from two decades on the hiring side.
Srikanth writes most weeks, usually about the same handful of things: presence, people skills, culture, and what actually separates a graduate who gets the offer from one who does not. A selection is below, in his own words.
Follow on LinkedIn Book a 15 minute intro call
Campus to Corporate
### CTRL + ALT + TRANSFORM: Classroom Confidence to Corporate Presence
The corporate world does not merely seek degrees, it seeks individuals who can communicate with confidence, adapt with agility, collaborate with purpose, and lead with authenticity. Just as a computer responds to CTRL + ALT + DELETE to reset, every student has the power to CTRL their mindset and choices, ALT their approach to challenges, and TRANSFORM their potential into professional excellence. The classroom is your launchpad. The corporate world is your runway.
Read the full post on LinkedIn →
People Skills Series
### Are You a People Magnet in Your Organization?
Every organization has a few individuals who seem to attract people effortlessly. They may not always hold the highest title, but they hold something even more powerful: influence, trust, and connection. People do not leave organizations; they leave environments where they do not feel connected, valued, or inspired. The true measure of leadership is not how many people work for you, but how many people grow because of you.
Read the full post on LinkedIn →
Leadership presence
### The First KPI When You Enter the Office Is Your Presence
Before productivity, profits, dashboards, or reports, ask yourself: did I greet people with positive energy, did I make someone feel valued, did I listen before I directed? Your first KPI is not Key Performance Indicator. It is Kindness, Presence, Influence. People may forget your instructions, but they rarely forget how you made them feel.
Read the full post on LinkedIn →
Culture and retention
### Culture Keeps Talent. Compensation Respects Talent.
Over the years I have seen employees who stayed despite attractive external offers, and employees who left organizations that paid exceptionally well. Once compensation reaches a reasonable level, employees begin asking deeper questions: do I feel valued here, am I learning and growing, does my leader inspire trust? The answers define culture. Compensation may attract talent. Culture may retain talent.
Read the full post on LinkedIn →
Learning and development
### Learning Alone Does Not Transform Organizations. Behaviour Does.
Organizations spend significant time and resources on learning initiatives, but the real question is how much of that learning shows up in everyday actions. Leadership brings credibility to learning by role-modelling the desired behaviours, and culture reinforces them by making them part of how things are done. Learning informs. Leadership inspires. Culture reinforces. Behaviour transforms.
Read the full post on LinkedIn →
Mindful leadership
### Most Leaders Are Running on Empty
We appear busy, productive, and successful on the outside. Yet beneath the titles, meetings, targets, and decisions, we are often operating with an empty state of mind. Not because we lack capability, but because we rarely pause to refill what leadership constantly demands: clarity, energy, perspective, and purpose. The challenge is not a lack of time; it is a lack of intentional renewal.
Read the full post on LinkedIn →
These are excerpts. The full posts, and everything written since, are on LinkedIn.

Title: Portfolio of Srikanth Kalyanasundaram, M.IOD | HR Leader
Description: Career history, frameworks, campus engagements, awards and a session gallery from a former mechanical engineer with over two decades in HR leadership.

The Person
# Srikanth Kalyanasundaram, M.IOD
Bridging the shop floor and the boardroom: over two decades of HR leadership, turning technical talent into confident professionals.
The Career Journey
## A personal path through the transition.
Srikanth began his career not in the boardroom, but on the factory shop floor. After completing a Diploma in Mechanical Engineering (Sandwich) from Coimbatore Institute of Technology (1986 to 1990), he worked hands-on at Kirloskar Pneumatics as Service-In-Charge, where the shop floor gave him the engineer's instinct for process he still brings to people work.
This early technical experience gave him a deep, practical understanding of engineering environments and workplace realities. In 1998, he made a strategic pivot into Human Resources with Owens Corning India, managing recruitment, compliance, and payroll. To back this transition with academic rigor, he earned a Post Graduate Diploma in HR Management from Welingkar Institute, Mumbai (2006 to 2008) while working full-time.
Since 2008, Srikanth has served at John Cockerill (most recently as Deputy General Manager of Human Resources), leading large-scale digital systems implementation (SAP SuccessFactors and HCM), executive compensation benchmarking, performance management frameworks, and flagship onboarding programmes.
Professional History

Title: Privacy Notice | Srikanth Kalyanasundaram
Description: How this website collects, uses and protects personal data under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and the rights you have.

Privacy
# Privacy notice.
What this website collects, why, and the rights you have under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
## Who is responsible
This website is run by Srikanth Kalyanasundaram, an individual based in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India, who is the Data Fiduciary for personal data collected through it. You can reach him about anything in this notice through the contact page or at mtmdselflove@gmail.com.
## What we collect
- Enquiry details you choose to send: your name, institution or company, email address, optional phone number, the kind of enquiry, and your message.
- Nothing else about you. The site sets no cookies, runs no analytics or advertising trackers, and does not build a profile of visitors.
- Display settings you pick (theme, text size, reduced motion) are saved only in your own browser and never sent to us.
## Why we use it
Only to reply to your enquiry and, if you go ahead, to arrange and deliver the session or engagement you asked about. We do not sell, rent or share your details for marketing, and we will not add you to a mailing list without asking separately.
## Your consent
We process enquiry details on the basis of your consent, which you give by ticking the box on the enquiry form. You can withdraw it at any time by writing to us; withdrawing does not affect anything already done before you withdrew.
## Who else handles it
The site is hosted on Cloudflare, and its fonts are served by Google Fonts, so those providers see the technical information any website visit involves (such as your IP address) under their own privacy policies. Enquiries sent through the form are delivered to our email inbox by FormSubmit (formsubmit.co), and our email is provided by Google (Gmail). Both handle the details you submit only to deliver and store them for us.
## How long we keep it
Enquiries that do not lead to work are deleted within 12 months. Records of work we deliver are kept for as long as Indian tax and accounting law requires, and then deleted.
## Your rights
Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 you can ask us to:
- tell you what personal data we hold about you and how it is used;
- correct, complete or update it;
- erase it, where we no longer need to keep it;
- nominate another person to exercise these rights on your behalf.
Write to us through the contact page. We aim to respond within 30 days. If you are not satisfied with our response, you can complain to the Data Protection Board of India.
## Children
This site is meant for institutions, companies and adult professionals. We do not knowingly collect personal data from anyone under 18. Colleges arranging sessions for students contact us as institutions.
## Changes to this notice
If this notice changes, the date below changes with it.
Last updated: 6 November 2026

Terms
# Terms of use.
The plain rules for using this website.
## About this website
This website describes training, coaching and advisory services offered by Srikanth Kalyanasundaram, based in Mumbai, India. By using it you agree to these terms.
## Information, not an offer
The content here is general information about the services. It is not a binding offer or professional advice. Scope, schedule and fees for any engagement are agreed in writing before work begins, and those written terms take precedence over anything on this site.
Employee benefits work is independent advice only. We do not sell, solicit or arrange insurance, and we take no commission from insurers or brokers.
## Fees and taxes
Fees are quoted per engagement in Indian rupees. Where GST applies, it is charged as required by law and shown on the invoice.
## Content and names
The text, programme structures, frameworks and photographs on this site belong to Srikanth Kalyanasundaram unless stated otherwise. You may share links and short quotes with credit; please ask before reusing anything else. Names of institutions and organisations are mentioned only to describe past sessions and do not imply endorsement.
## Testimonials
Quotes on this site are reproduced from public recommendations given by the named people, with the date they were written. They describe those people's own experience.

Links to LinkedIn and other websites are provided for convenience. We are not responsible for their content or privacy practices.

We work to keep this site accurate and available, but it is provided as it is. To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for losses arising from its use.

## Grievances
